items.title: C-MoA-XRT: Explainability-Aware Trust Routing for Collaborative Threat Detection in Mobile-Edge Networks
items.abstract: Threat detection in mobile-edge networks requires reliable inference from heterogeneous telemetry whose availability and evidential quality may vary over time. LLM-assisted detectors further introduce uncertainty because prediction confidence may not reflect evidence trustworthiness, while collaborative reasoning can amplify unsupported decisions. This paper proposes C-MoA-XRT, a trust-aware collaborative Mixture-of-Agents framework for resilient mobile-edge threat detection. C-MoA-XRT distributes complementary network evidence across specialized LLM agents and performs event-specific trust routing before collaborative inference. The proposed routing mechanism separates prediction confidence from decision authority by assessing the reliability, consistency, and evidential support of each specialist output. A defensive red-team reasoning stage subsequently examines the fused evidence, while an evidence-anchored decision firewall constrains unstable collaborative reasoning from overriding the calibrated detection outcome. Experiments on NF-UNSW-NB15 show that C-MoA-XRT achieves an F1 score of 0.900 with full attack recall and reduces the false-positive rate by approximately 75% relative to the evaluated single-agent RAG+LLM baseline. Under measurement drift, trust-aware evidence gating improves PR-AUC from 0.694 to 0.917 over confidence-based routing, while maintaining resilience under the evaluated telemetry-dropout and unreliable-specialist conditions. These results demonstrate that explicit control of evidence trust and reasoning authority can improve the robustness of collaborative LLM-based threat detection in mobile-edge networks.

items.title: Continuous Semantic Caching for Low-Cost LLM Serving
items.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become increasingly popular, caching responses so that they can be reused by users with semantically similar queries has become a vital strategy for reducing inference costs and latency. Existing caching frameworks have proposed to decide which query responses to cache by assuming a finite, known universe of discrete queries and learning their serving costs and arrival probabilities. As LLMs' pool of users and queries expands, however, such an assumption becomes increasingly untenable: real-world LLM queries reside in an infinite, continuous embedding space. In this paper, we establish the first rigorous theoretical framework for semantic LLM response caching in continuous query space under uncertainty. To bridge the gap between discrete optimization and continuous representation spaces, we introduce dynamic e-net discretization coupled with Kernel Ridge Regression. This design enables the system to formally quantify estimation uncertainty and generalize partial feedback on LLM query costs across continuous semantic query neighborhoods. We develop both offline learning and online adaptive algorithms optimized to reduce switching costs incurred by changing the cached responses. We prove that our online algorithm achieves a sublinear regret bound against an optimal oracle, which reduces to existing bounds for discrete query models. Extensive empirical evaluations demonstrate that our framework approximates the continuous optimal cache well while also reducing computational and switching overhead compared to existing methods.

items.title: Demo: Multimodal Stress Monitoring with Split Federated Fine-Tuning on Mobile Devices
items.abstract: We present an end-to-end mobile system for proactive stress monitoring from wearable signals. The framework is supported by an extensible split federated learning system that enables on-device LoRA fine-tuning of large language models. By analyzing physiological data, the application distinguishes emotional states, summarizes recent trends, and provides brief, actionable suggestions. Upon detecting a negative emotional state, the paired smartwatch or smartphone proactively delivers notifications to users to encourage mindfulness. The on-site demonstration will showcase real-time sensing-inference on smartwatch-phone pairs, alongside a recorded split federated learning process that continuously learns from user private data. Our code has been open-sourced at: https://github.com/HKU-WILL-Lab/Multimodal-Stress-Monitoring-with-Split-Federated-Fine-Tuning-on-Mobile-Devices.

items.title: Demo: On-Device Agent for Personalized and Efficient Mobile Network Configuration
items.abstract: As mobile devices increasingly operate across heterogeneous access networks and diverse usage contexts, efficient network configuration requires decisions that adapt to both dynamic network conditions and individual user preferences. We demonstrate an on-device communication agent that transforms historical user network-switching behavior into personalized configuration rules. An on-device Large language model (LLM) analyzes switching records offline and generates condition-action rules capturing recurring user preferences. During real-time use, the agent retrieves matched rules locally and executes the corresponding network configuration after user confirmation, without invoking the LLM. Attendees will choose a prepared behavior trace, inspect the rule generated on the phone, and recreate its triggering context to observe an immediate network switch. The demonstration shows how separating deliberation from execution makes personalized mobile network configuration both interpretable and responsive while keeping user data and inference on the device.

items.title: Demo: Vision-Language Model-Guided Online Calibration of an Electromagnetic Digital Twin
items.abstract: An electromagnetic (EM) digital twin gives mobile robots wireless situational awareness but depends on material conductivities that change with the environment. Online calibration faces initialization sensitivity and measurement travel costs. We demonstrate a vision-language model (VLM)-guided framework using a Unitree G1 robot and NVIDIA Sionna, with two VLM calls: material classification maps visible materials through ITU-R P.2040 to conductivity priors for Sionna's gradient descent on accumulated received signal strength (RSS) measurements; waypoint planning selects the next measurement location online using residual RSS calibration error and image coverage. In a real indoor scenario, the framework achieves a normalized mean absolute conductivity error of 1.74 × 10-4 within 20 m of travel; random initialization never converges, while random waypoints require over twice the travel.

items.title: Foundation Model-Aided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Wireless Random Access Network Optimization
items.abstract: Random access (RA) is one of the most foundational medium access control (MAC) layer scheduling schemes for handling unpredictable data traffic from multiple terminals. While multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has been explored to optimize RA-based wireless networks, its reliance on experience-driven, distributed policy learning incurs significant training overhead for each optimization task, limiting its feasibility in real-world applications. In this work, we propose to leverage a foundation model (FM) to improve MARL efficiency across diverse RA network optimization tasks. Specifically, we design an FM-aided actor-critic algorithm within a consensus-based decentralized MARL architecture and provide its convergence analysis under local reward exchanges and nonlinear value function approximations to show that our algorithm achieves the same convergence order as the conventional MARL with critic model exchanges and linear approximations. Our numerical results show that our FM-based approach significantly enhances MARL speed for RA network optimization.

items.title: FrozenSFL: Model-Frozen Split Federated Learning for Resource-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning over Heterogeneous Edge Devices
items.abstract: Collaborative fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) at the network edge enables privacy-preserving and personalized generative intelligence, but is constrained by the limited memory and compute resources of edge devices. Traditional approaches, such as split federated learning (SFL), partition models between devices and a server, requiring iterative exchanges of activations/gradients while the server manages multiple submodels. This leads to substantial communication overhead, high activation storage costs, and severe server-side memory pressure when scaling to massive heterogeneous devices. In this paper, we propose FrozenSFL, a resource-efficient SFL framework for collaborative fine-tuning of LLMs across heterogeneous edge devices. At its core, FrozenSFL strictly freezes device-side submodels to eliminate both deviceside backpropagation and server-to-device gradient transmission, thereby removing on-device activation storage requirements and downlink communication overhead. Building upon this design, we improve the framework in two aspects. First, we design a layerwise LoRA aggregation strategy to handle structural heterogeneity introduced by device-specific model partitioning and enable efficient server-side updates. Second, we introduce a server-side feature caching mechanism that reuses invariant features, allowing subsequent training epochs to proceed offline and reducing redundant computation and communication. We implement the FrozenSFL system as an asynchronous multi-threaded pipeline, which serves as our real-world testbed for evaluation. On the device side, forward computation and data transmission are decoupled via a producer-consumer mechanism. On the server side, a first-in-first-out scheduling strategy serializes fine-tuning tasks across devices. A hybrid memory-disk streaming mechanism further buffers incoming data and ensures stable training under network variability. Extensive evaluations with representative models, including BERT-Base (0.11B), ViT-Large (0.3B), and LLaMA-2-7B (7B), validate the effectiveness of FrozenSFL. In particular, for LLaMA-2-7B, FrozenSFL can reduce device/server VRAM footprint by up to 14%/82.7% with only 1% accuracy loss, while achieving up to 6.7× fine-tuning speedup.

items.title: Just Talk Once: Communication-Efficient Split Federated LLM Fine-Tuning on Edge Devices
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) fine-tuning is increasingly shifting toward data generated on edge devices, where memory, computation, bandwidth, and connectivity constraints make conventional federated learning difficult to sustain. Split federated fine-tuning (SFT) improves client-side efficiency by offloading most model parameters and computation to the server but requires step-by-step bidirectional communication loop across the split interface and forces continuous client involvement throughout training. In this paper, we present L-shaped SFT, a split fine-tuning framework that removes this bidirectional bottleneck. Our key insight is that weight tying in modern LLMs enables server-side hidden activations to be directly supervised using target embeddings, allowing the training loss to be computed on the server without returning server outputs to the client. To further eliminate the need for continuous client participation, based on L-shaped SFT, we introduce one-shot SFT, in which clients upload activations once and then go offline while the server continues optimization over cached representations. We implement our design in a real system testbed with heterogeneous edge clients, including commercial smartphones and NVIDIA developer boards. Experiments demonstrate that our schemes significantly reduce communication costs and client online time compared with existing SFT baselines.

items.title: LLM-Enabled Self-Organizing UAV Networks for Autonomous Service Provisioning
items.abstract: The growing demand for flexible and resilient low-altitude connectivity is driving UAV networks toward increasingly autonomous operation. However, existing approaches often assume known user distributions, fixed network configurations, or treat exploration, access, and backhaul separately, resulting in a gap between user discovery and end-to-end service in initially unknown environments. To address this challenge, we propose a self-organizing heterogeneous UAV networking framework, referred to as Discovery-to-Service (D2S) Network, that supports the complete process from user discovery to end-to-end service provisioning. The framework adopts a dual-timescale coordination mechanism: at the fast timescale, onboard graph reinforcement learning agents perform user exploration and local control, while at the slower timescale, a basestation-hosted LLM reconfigures the access and backhaul infrastructure based on discovered demands and the global network state. Experiments over 42 scenarios show that, compared with a heuristic connectivity-constrained grid-greedy method, the proposed framework improves effective coverage by 23.38 percentage points, terminal throughput by 55.3%, and cumulative throughput by 44.3%, demonstrating its effectiveness for autonomous network formation under unknown demand.

items.title: MIRA: An Edge-Cloud Multimodal LLM Framework for DESH Assessment in IoT-Enabled MRI Workflows
items.abstract: Connected MRI scanners operate as networked medical devices within DICOM-based healthcare Internet of Things (IoT) workflows, but conventional connectivity primarily moves images to a Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) rather than adding task-specific reasoning near acquisition. Building on DESH-App 2.0, a preceding machine-learning contribution accepted for oral presentation at SIN Firenze 2026, this paper specifies MIRA (Multimodal Imaging Reasoning and Assessment), a vendor-neutral edge-cloud module for assessing disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid spaces (DESH). A hospital-edge gateway validates and de-identifies 3D T1-weighted DICOM studies, derives ventricular, high-convexity, and Sylvian-fissure masks with SegFormer3D, and converts each volume into a compact evidence package comprising 12 representative slices with overlays, 17 global, zonal, and ratio features, and quality-control tokens. LLaVA-Med-7B and Lingshu-7B are adapted through 4-bit QLoRA to return constrained JSON containing class, confidence, named anatomical evidence, and an abstention or quality warning. The edge-cloud partition keeps raw volumes inside the institutional network; only the compact evidence package may reach an authenticated inference service, while structured outputs return to the PACS workstation. The evaluation protocol jointly covers diagnostic discrimination, calibration, evidence agreement, unsupported claims, abstention, latency, transmitted bytes, memory demand, link-loss recovery, and multi-device interoperability. MIRA is designed to add auditable multimodal reasoning to connected MRI workflows without modifying safety-critical scanner controls.

items.title: POLAR: Online Learning for LoRA Adapter Caching and Routing in Edge LLM Serving
items.abstract: Edge deployment of large language models (LLMs) increasingly relies on libraries of lightweight LoRA adapters, yet GPU/DRAM can keep only a small resident subset at a time. Serving a request through a non-resident adapter requires paging its weights from storage, incurring measurable latency. This creates a two-timescale online control problem: on a slow timescale, the system selects which adapters remain resident in fast memory, while on a fast timescale it routes each request to an adapter whose context-dependent utility is unknown a priori. The two decisions are tightly coupled: the cache determines the cost of exploration, and the router determines which adapters receive informative feedback. We formulate this joint caching-and-routing problem as a two-timescale contextual bandit and propose POLAR (Paging and Online Learning for Adapter Routing). POLAR pairs a cache-aware LinUCB router with an epoch-based cache controller. We study two variants. A fixed-epoch version provides a robust baseline with worst-case regret guarantees under arbitrary contexts. An epoch-doubling version, POLAR+, adds forced exploration and improved cache optimization to achieve O~(dNT+KT) sublinear regret under stochastic regularity and cacheability conditions, where N is the adapter count, K the cache size, d the context dimension, and T the horizon. The routing term matches the standard contextual-bandit rate up to logarithmic factors, showing that the memory hierarchy does not fundamentally slow routing learning. Experiments using 15 real LoRA adapters for Qwen2.5-7B together with measured GPU paging latencies show that adaptive cache control substantially outperforms heuristic caching baselines.

items.title: Axiological Problems of Artificial Intelligence in Education: Between Technological Efficiency and the Humanization of Learning
items.abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education offers opportunities to improve efficiency, personalize learning, and support educational activities. However, these benefits raise an axiological question concerning the extent to which technological efficiency contributes to meaningful learning and human development. This article examines the axiological problems associated with the use of AI in education, particularly the tension between technological efficiency and the humanization of learning. Using a literature review approach, this study synthesizes scholarly literature to examine educational values, pedagogical implications, and ethical considerations in AI integration. Through thematic comparison, the synthesis identifies recurring issues and conceptual relationships among the instrumental benefits of AI, student agency, pedagogical relationships, and ethical responsibilities in its use. These relationships are integrated into a conceptual framework comprising four interconnected dimensions: instrumental value, student agency, pedagogical relationships, and ethical-contextual responsibility. The framework emphasizes that the educational value of AI cannot be determined solely by efficiency or the automation of learning activities, but should be assessed in terms of students’ independent thinking, the quality of pedagogical interactions, and ethical principles and contextual needs. This study offers an axiological perspective that connects these four dimensions to evaluate AI adoption in education, positioning technological efficiency as one consideration rather than the sole criterion of educational value. Since the proposed framework is developed through a conceptual synthesis of literature, further research is needed to examine its applicability across different educational contexts.

items.title: Fact-Checking Journalism Practices Against Health Disinformation: A Content Analysis of Teyit.org (2023–2026)
items.abstract: This study examines the fact-checking content published in the health category by Teyit.org, an IFCN-verified fact-checking platform based in Turkey, between 1 January 2023 and 30 June 2026, through observable indicators associated with professional journalistic norms. Unlike the tendency observed in the literature reviewed, the research analyses not disinformation content but the fact-checking platform’s own editorial practices. A full census of all items meeting the criteria (N = 100) was conducted, and source diversity, transparency, forms of evidence presentation, language and style features and disclosures concerning the use of artificial intelligence (AI) were coded through quantitative content analysis. The findings show that the content verification process is primarily based on official documents, expert opinions and technical data, and that question-form headings are widely used. The use of evidence varied depending on how claims were presented, but the use of expert opinions did not differ significantly across health subtopics. The analysis also found that the content generally avoided emotional and dramatic language. Given the widespread impact of the ‘post-truth’ era today, this finding is considered significant in that it demonstrates that the content has been examined using an evidence-based and more measured approach to verification. Editorial disclosures about AI use became more frequent only in the final part of the study period. This coincided with the platform’s introduction of an AI attribution standard in March 2026. These findings suggest that disclosures about AI use became more visible as part of editorial transparency in Teyit.org’s health-related content. In conclusion, this study suggests that fact-checking journalism in the content examined serves a purpose beyond correcting false information. Although the relationship between fact-checking and public trust was not examined in this study, fact-checking journalism can be understood, within the specific context of Teyit.org and the health category, as a form of journalism whose observable indicators are consistent with the norms of accuracy, transparency, and accountability in digital journalism.

items.title: Model choice and prompt framing in LLM sustainability judgments
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for sustainability assessment and decision support, yet their judgments may depend on the selected model and on how the task is defined. We compare 13 locally executed open-weight LLMs on 80 author-written sustainability scenarios using three prompt families that ask which actor should be responsible, bear the costs, or initiate action. Each model answered at two temperature settings with 100 repetitions, producing 624,000 deposited outputs, of which 610,708 contain a complete score vector. Scores were analyzed as relative actor support after removing each response’s overall level. Within this instrument, the cost prompt family produced the highest cross-model disagreement, exceeding both responsibility and catalyst by 7.37 points (question-cluster 95% intervals 5.56−9.15 and 5.38−9.36, describing variation across these 80 scenarios). It also produced the most lead-actor disagreement and the lowest full consensus. Moving from catalyst to cost reduced relative support for government and increased it for individuals and firms; moving from cost to responsibility largely reversed this pattern. These differences exceeded temperature-setting differences and persisted under model exclusion, alternative score transformations and tie rules, missing-response checks, and stems without explicit cost wording. Exploratory category patterns are conditional on uneven item coverage. Secondary rationale-language comparisons show the same within-model ordering but not the most cross-model variation under cost. Operational use should disclose model, prompt, and temperature choices; compare plausible alternatives; repeat generations; and refer high-disagreement judgments for human deliberation.

items.title: The Effects of AI Readiness, HRM Practices, and Continuous Learning Culture on HR Analytics Capability in Public Service Organizations
items.abstract: The study aims to investigate the effect of AI Readiness, HRM Practices and Continuous Learning Culture to HR Analytics Capability in public sector enterprises in Indonesia. The research was conducted based on a quantitative approach and the survey technique. The research participants consisted of the workers of public sector organizations who have expertise in the use of digital information systems and management of personnel data. The data were collected using an online questionnaire through Google Forms. The questions used a five-point Likert scale. The sampling technique used purposive sampling. Multiple linear regression was used to explore HR Analytics Capability in relation to the three independent variables. The proposed study model indicates that AI Readiness, HRM Practices and Continuous Learning Culture are positively related to HR Analytics Capability. AI Readiness is expected to have the highest relative impact. Artificial intelligence preparation may enhance the organizational capacity to integrate, analyze and use personnel data. Quality information is available with good human resource management practices. Moreover, a culture of continuous learning promotes the enhancement of employees’ analytical skills, teamwork and flexibility. The report provides practical implications for public service companies in terms of the value of strengthening AI infrastructure, data quality, digital competences, human resource management practices and promoting a culture of continuous learning for achieving HR Analytics Capability.

items.title: THE EVOLUTION AND ETHICAL INTEGRATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN MODERN EDUCATION: A FRAMEWORK FOR PERSONALIZED LEARNING AND INSTITUTIONAL ACCOUNTABILITY
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has come a long way from its early theoretical days in the mid -1950s to become an advanced, data-based system that can learn from experience and execute jobs automatically. At present times, AI acts as a game-changer in education by making possible customized educational experiences based on the use of machine learning frameworks that provide individual guidance to every student, taking into account their speed, behaviour, preferences, and accomplishments. The change of this technological nature means that the role of a teacher must be shifted to the one who should now only provide guidance and help in, additionally, overseeing the machines. Beyond classrooms, AI adoption is a priority for national policies. For instance, India’s National Education Policy 2020 requires the teaching of AI and computational thinking in schools. The curriculum is set to start from Grade 3 in the academic year 2026-27. However, the rise of AI may create some challenges in terms of socio-economics. While AIED researchers are usually driven by the goals of enhancing learning results, the experience from other fields of AI indicates that good intentions do not guarantee ethical use of the technology. Important issues such as data ownership, algorithm bias, transparency, and student agency still remain unresolved. There is a necessity of collaborative endeavours in the creation of a community-wide framework in addressing the difference between "doing ethical things" and "doing things ethically. The PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) framework is a prominent method for ensuring transparency and repeatability in systematic reviews and can be used in the mapping of the enormous literature in this evolving sphere, while the mentioned resources mainly rely on expert surveys of leading scientists to define the major shortcomings.

items.title: Trust in Machine Learning-Aided Docking: A Systematic Review of Good Practices for Chemically Reliable Predictions
items.abstract: The massive growth of chemical libraries presents both an opportunity and a challenge in large-scale virtual screening. Machine learning (ML) algorithms have successfully accelerated this process with surrogate docking models that learn patterns between molecular representations and docking scores for ranking undocked molecules. Deep learning (DL), which represents the majority of ML-boosted docking approaches, has a sophisticated capability of finding nonlinear, complex relationships in voluminous data. However, DL algorithms operate as black boxes, face difficulties in generalization and raise concerns on whether correct predictions are, in fact, made for causal relationships between chemical structure and biological activity. Candidate molecules cannot be confidently tested if predictions are not understandable in human terms. The lack of understanding of relevant chemical properties impairs compound discovery, optimization and novelty, reinforcing the high-risk and high-cost scenario of drug design. To offer insights for expanding the recent breakthroughs achieved with the docking/ML integration, this review included 57 ML-aided docking papers from January 2020 to August 2026. We assessed how ML predictions are generated, refined and chemically interpreted to reliably reduce docking simulations and ideally increase experimental hit rates by data-driven and expert-driven decisions on compound selection. On this matter, the proper implementation of eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques is informative to elucidate if and how trustworthy are predicted hits from a chemical perspective, assuring a safer and more effective decision-making process for finding true hits. Nonetheless, only four (7.0%) out of 57 papers applied XAI techniques, mostly involving feature attribution methods, but not the state-of-the-art contrastive explanations method. Therefore, the implementation of XAI in ML-boosted docking is still scarce and needs formalization to avoid misinterpreting results. We review the various opportunities and limitations for integrating ML-aided docking with XAI techniques alongside complementary trust-enhancing strategies present in the included studies, such as sampling strategies, target diversity, ensemble and consensus docking, active learning, ensemble models, physicochemical and pharmacophore-based filtering, multiobjective optimization of molecular properties, confidence metrics of predefined acceptable errors, and expected model improvement along iterations. Given the broad applications of XAI across scientific domains and proof-of-concept studies in computational chemistry, we believe benchmarking and combining current and novel trust-enhancing strategies in ML-aided docking can go beyond finding initial hits. It supports both the statistical assessment including XAI in predictions and the mechanistic understanding of chemically relevant drug candidates for transparent and credible model and drug development.

items.title: When Humanlike AI Feels Wrong: Perceived Eeriness and Trust in AI-Mediated Brand Communication — A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Background: This review examines when humanlike artificial intelligence (AI) becomes unsettling and how uncanny appraisal relates to consumer trust in AI-mediated brand communication. It integrates the trust-building logic of anthropomorphism with evidence of unfavorable trust-related evaluations under uncanny conditions. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 and SPAR-4-SLR principles, a Scopus search identified 7,665 records. After duplicate, document-type, and title/abstract screening, 18 journal articles were retained, verified in full text, and coded by AI form, appraisal mechanism, trust object, boundary condition, outcome, and evidence directness. Additional theoretical sources were used for conceptual anchoring but were not added to the systematic evidence corpus. Results: Five studies provide direct uncanny-appraisal evidence, six proximal-appraisal evidence, and seven contextual anthropomorphism–trust evidence. Direct studies associate unfavorable uncanny appraisal with lower trust-related evaluation, using distinct measures of affect, trust, and source trustworthiness. Human-likeness is not inherently harmful: social cues can support trust when aligned with competence, empathy, usefulness, transparency, and task demands. Conclusion: The review develops the Eeriness-Trust Calibration Framework (ETCF), separating design cues from consumer appraisals, positive and negative trust routes, and multiple trust objects. It reframes AI humanization as a cue-capability-context calibration problem and identifies cross-object trust transfer to organizations and brands as a key unresolved marketing mechanism. Brands should optimize coherence rather than maximize realism, pretest eeriness and authenticity together, and monitor trust separately at agent, content, provider, and brand levels.

items.title: 5. ve 6. Sınıf Ortaokul Öğrencilerinin Yapay Zekâya Yönelik Anlayışlarının Belirlenmesine İlişkin Durum Çalışması
items.abstract: Bu araştırmanın amacı, 5. ve 6. sınıf ortaokul öğrencilerinin yapay zekâ kavramına, çalışma mantığına, insan zekâsı ile ilişkisine, günlük yaşamdaki kullanımına, olası yarar ve zararlarına ve öğretmenin yerini alabilme potansiyeline ilişkin anlayışlarını bütüncül ve karşılaştırmalı olarak incelemektir. Nitel araştırma yaklaşımlarından durum çalışması deseninin benimsendiği çalışmanın çalışma grubunu, Mersin ilinde bulunan ortaokullarda öğrenim gören toplam 218 beşinci ve altıncı sınıf öğrencisi oluşturmaktadır. Katılımcılar kolay ulaşılabilir (uygun) örnekleme yöntemiyle belirlenmiştir. Araştırmanın verileri, katılımcıların demografik niteliklerini belirleyen sorular ile yapay zekâya ilişkin algı, bilgi ve değerlendirmelerini derinlemesine ortaya koymayı amaçlayan açık uçlu sorulardan oluşan anket formu aracılığıyla toplanmıştır. Elde edilen nitel verilerin çözümlenmesinde içerik analizi tekniği kullanılmış; temalar, kodlar ve frekans dağılımları oluşturulmuştur. Yapay zekânın çalışma mekanizmasına yönelik olarak 5. sınıfların donanım altyapısı ve dikkat çekici biçimde su tüketimi gibi çevresel faktörlere odaklandığı, 6. sınıfların ise insan ve kuruluşların rolü, veri işleme, soru-cevap etkileşimi ve kodlama süreçlerini öne çıkardığı belirlenmiştir. items.title: A comparative study of vision foundation models for few-shot classification in benthic imagery
items.abstract: Benthic imagery constitutes a primary data source for studying seafloor habitats, providing rich visual information essential for ecological assessment and marine ecosystem monitoring. Recent advances in underwater robotic platforms have substantially increased the capacity for large-scale benthic image acquisition, shifting the primary bottleneck from data collection to image annotation and analysis. However, manual annotation of benthic imagery remains labor-intensive, time-consuming, and dependent on domain expertise, limiting the scalability of marine habitat analysis. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted annotation tools have shown promise, their application to benthic imagery remains challenging due to the substantial domain gap between underwater imagery and conventional terrestrial computer vision datasets. In addition, annotated benthic datasets are often limited in size, geographically sparse, and highly imbalanced. Few-shot learning (FSL) offers a promising solution by enabling rapid adaptation to new datasets using only a small number of labeled examples. In this work, we propose a foundation-model-based few-shot classification (FSC) framework for benthic imagery annotation. The proposed framework uses pretrained visual representations and systematically investigates the influence of backbone family, model scale, support-set construction strategy, and adaptation algorithm under limited labeled-data conditions. Furthermore, we investigate a prioritized support-set construction strategy based on embedding-space clustering to improve annotation efficiency in low-shot regimes. Experimental results across three benthic imagery datasets demonstrate that DINOv3 ViT-S/16 provides the strongest overall classification performance among the evaluated backbone families, while increasing backbone size does not consistently improve accuracy. LinearSVC also demonstrates strong and consistent adaptation performance across the datasets. In addition, the proposed prioritized labeling strategy improves classification accuracy compared with class-balanced random sampling on Datasets B and C, with average gains of 7.62 and 5.02 percentage points, respectively, and corresponding 95% confidence intervals excluding zero, while the improvement on Dataset A is inconclusive. However, these accuracy gains do not consistently translate into higher macro-averaged F1 scores, highlighting the dataset-dependent effects of representative sample selection. Beyond classification performance, this work introduces an annotation-time modeling framework to analyze the practical deployment trade-offs of few-shot benthic annotation workflows. Under the evaluated annotation-time assumptions, FSC is estimated to reduce overall annotation time by 6.7% and 21.7% on Datasets A and B, respectively, compared with traditional fine-tuning approaches. On Dataset C, traditional fine-tuning shows only a small and uncertain estimated advantage of 1.3%. Overall, the results suggest that DINOv3-based few-shot classification provides an effective low-label annotation-support approach, with potential annotation-time advantages that depend on dataset size, classification accuracy, and annotation costs.

items.title: A comprehensive review of biosignal foundation models
items.abstract: Objective. Foundation models are emerging as a promising approach to biosignal analysis, offering solutions to common challenges in learning from biosignal data, such as high variability, noise or limited annotations. This survey provides a comprehensive review of the state-of-the-art in this rapidly advancing field. Approach. We introduce commonly used biosignal modalities (including electroencephalography, electrocardiography, electromyography, electrooculography and photoplethysmography) and discuss their defining characteristics with respect to training large models. Main results. We present a structured survey of existing work across unimodal and multimodal settings covering data processing, feature extraction, model architectures, pre-training paradigms and evaluation methods. We identify open challenges such as benchmarking, interpretability and data availability and highlight possible directions for future research. Significance. By consolidating our findings from the current literature and opportunities for progress, we aim to guide the development of robust and universal foundation models for biosignals.

items.title: A Digital Stress Resilience Model for Sustainable Performance and Responsible Organizations
items.abstract: The rapid Digitalization of organizational work, accelerated by Artificial Intelligence, hybrid work, ubiquitous connectivity, and continuous information exchange, has created unprece dented opportunities for productivity. Simultaneously the issues of intensifying digital overload, cognitive fatigue, work interruptions, technostress, and emotional exhaustion have been non-trivial challenges for organizations. Existing organizational stress-management approaches predominantly emphasize individual coping or post-stress interventions and provide limited integration of real-time Digital Stress detection, adaptive regulation, responsible technology governance, and sustainable productivity. Addressing the above challenges and the research gap, we propose a Digital Stress Resilience Model grounded in Sustainable Positive Computing, Self-awareness, Affective Computing, Organizational Psychology, and Responsible Artificial intelligence. Our proposed model conceptualizes Digital Stress Management as a continuous socio-technical process comprising five interconnected capabilities such as Digital Stress Perception, Cognitive-Emotional Intelligence, Adaptive Stress Regulation, Responsible Digital Governance, and Resilience-Oriented Productivity Management. The model provides a conceptual roadmap for transforming organizations from reactive stress-management environments into proactive, self-aware, resilient, responsible, and productive digital workplaces. A mixed-method research design is proposed for subsequent empirical validation using digital workload, cognitive load, emotional regulation, resilience, responsible technology use, employee engagement, and sustainable productivity indicators.

items.title: A Human-Centric Decision Framework for Selecting Artificial Intelligence Collaboration Strategies Under Uncertainty in Industry 5.0
items.abstract: Effective collaboration between humans and artificial intelligence (AI) in industry 5.0 demands technological systems with human social-cognitive processes, such as trust calibration and shared mental model. This study introduces human-centric decision-making framework for configuring human-AI collaboration in smart manufacturing systems. As Industry 5.0 evolves, finding the best synergy between human intelligence and collaborative robots (cobots) becomes crucial for enhancing adaptability, safety, efficiency, and sustainability. The proposed methodology uses neutrosophic Z-numbers (NZN) to capture uncertainty with three components: truth, indeterminacy, and falsity with their associated reliabilities, and the NZN weighted arithmetic averaging (NZNWAA) operator to combine individual preferences of decision-makers. Afterward, the criteria importance through intercriteria correlation (CRITIC) method is used to objectively determine the importance of each criterion by analyzing contrast intensity and inter-criteria correlation. The ranking of alternatives is then obtained using the compromise ranking of alternatives from distance to ideal solution (CRADIS) method. This hybrid NZN-CRITIC-CRADIS approach is applied to a real-world case study of BMW manufacturing systems, assessing four human-AI collaboration strategies: full AI automation, partial cobot integration, human-led AI-assisted assembly, and hybrid multi-agent collaboration, across four critical criteria. The results of the study show that the AI-assisted assembly emerges as the most suitable solution, balancing technological capability with human-centric design. The effectiveness of the proposed approach has been further validated through a sensitivity analysis and a comparative assessment with existing decision-making techniques, where our model consistently demonstrated superior performance in handling uncertainty and maintaining objectivity. Ultimately, this study offers a reliable human-centered framework that emphasizes socially intelligent manufacturing.

items.title: A Hybrid Machine Learning System for Low-Cost, Interpretable Bend, Connector, and Break Detection in OTDR Traces
items.abstract: Reliable and rapid detection of physical events along fiber-optic communication lines is essential for maintaining the availability of power-grid infrastructure. However, conventional threshold-based optical time-domain reflectometry (OTDR) analysis is hampered by weak or gradual event signatures, and modern deep-learning alternatives are often too computationally demanding for low-cost field deployment. This study presents a hybrid machine learning system for automated, interpretable detection and classification of bend, connector, and break events in OTDR traces. The system combines a dense sliding-window branch, adapted to the gradual, spatially diffuse attenuation caused by fiber bending, with a sparse candidate-generation-and-classification branch based on an ExtraTrees ensemble for the more localized connector and break events. The pipeline, together with a purpose-built annotation tool (OTDR Studio), was implemented with a Gamma Lite OTDR, a Raspberry Pi 4 for trace acquisition and transmission, and a host computer for event detection. Before splitting, all traces were assigned to heuristic measurement groups, the annotations of eight byte-identical traces were reconciled, and both branches were retrained. The system obtained a pooled (micro-averaged) event-level precision of 0.918, recall of 0.784, and F1-score of 0.846 (inverse-group-size-weighted F1-score of 0.862), on a group-level held-out test set of 81 traces with 227 reference events. Class-aware non-maximum suppression, selected on the validation set, raised the test F1-score from 0.758 (class-agnostic suppression with the same models and thresholds) to 0.846; most remaining errors are missed connector events. The system is intended as a physically grounded, interpretable tool for technicians without machine-learning expertise; standalone operation on the Raspberry Pi and field validation are future work.

items.title: A Hybrid VAE–GAN Generative Artificial Intelligence Framework for De Novo Molecular Design, Novel Drug Candidate Generation, and Pharmaceutical Lead Optimization
items.abstract: The discovery and optimization of novel drug candidates remain significant challenges in pharmaceutical research due to the enormous chemical search space, high development costs, and complex molecular property requirements. This study presents a hybrid Variational Autoencoder–Generative Adversarial Network (VAE–GAN) framework for de novo molecular design, novel drug candidate generation, and pharmaceutical lead optimization. The proposed framework integrates the latent-space learning capabilities of a Variational Autoencoder with the adversarial training mechanism of a Generative Adversarial Network to enhance molecular generation, structural diversity, and physicochemical property optimization. The ZINC dataset, comprising 250,000 molecular structures represented as canonical Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (SMILES) strings, was employed for model development, while ChEMBL was incorporated for external molecular evaluation. Molecular preprocessing included structural standardization, duplicate removal, and dataset partitioning to ensure data consistency and reliable model assessment. The generated molecules were evaluated using chemical validity, uniqueness, novelty, internal diversity, quantitative estimate of drug-likeness (QED), and synthetic accessibility score (SAS). The hybrid VAE–GAN framework achieved 96.8% molecular validity, 94.1% uniqueness, and 89.5% novelty, demonstrating its capacity to generate chemically plausible and structurally distinct molecular candidates. Furthermore, the proposed model obtained an average QED score of 0.71, a synthetic accessibility score of 2.8, and an internal diversity score of 0.84, outperforming the standalone VAE baseline, which recorded corresponding values of 0.63, 3.4, and 0.77. Property-guided latent-space optimization further increased the proportion of molecules satisfying predefined drug-likeness criteria from 57.2% to 73.6%, indicating improved molecular optimization performance. These findings highlight the effectiveness of integrating variational representation learning and adversarial optimization for generating diverse, drug-like molecular structures while maintaining favorable synthetic accessibility characteristics. The proposed computational framework provides a scalable and promising approach for molecular exploration, virtual compound library generation, and pharmaceutical lead identification. Overall, this research demonstrates the potential of hybrid generative artificial intelligence architectures to accelerate early-stage drug discovery and support the development of novel therapeutic candidates through computationally guided molecular design and optimization strategies.

items.abstract: This study examines the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital games in the contemporary era. The digital gaming industry is continuously evolving under the influence of technological advancements, and AI is one of the most significant drivers of this transformation. In digital games, AI is applied in numerous areas, including improving the behavior of non-player characters (NPCs), dynamically adjusting difficulty levels, generating game content, and personalizing the player experience. The aim of this study is to investigate the areas in which AI is used in digital games and to evaluate its impact on the player experience. A literature review method was employed, and the development and application areas of AI in the digital gaming industry were analyzed. The findings indicate that AI technologies enhance the realism of games, strengthen player interaction, and contribute substantially to replay ability. Furthermore, AI-supported systems were found to increase user satisfaction by offering players more personalized and dynamic experiences. According to the findings, AI technologies play a strategic role in the development of digital games. In the future, AI will remain one of the key factors shaping game design and the player experience. Accordingly, greater investment by game developers in AI-based solutions will enable them to gain a competitive advantage within the industry.

items.title: A pilot survey of clinician perspectives on an ambient AI scribe in two emergency departments
items.abstract: Objective Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes are being adopted to reduce clinical documentation burden, but evidence from the emergency department (ED), a high-acuity, frequently interrupted setting, remains limited. We evaluated ED clinicians' perceptions of an ambient AI documentation platform (Ambience) implemented across two EDs in one United States health system, using a two-round cross-sectional survey and inductive qualitative content analysis of free-text responses. Results Twenty-three clinicians provided 34 responses. All responses (100%) reported high overall satisfaction, willingness to recommend the platform, and enhanced focus during patient encounters; enhanced documentation quality and improved work-life balance were each reported in 32 of 34 responses (94%). Among 18 responses from clinicians with prior human-scribe experience, 16 (89%) used a human scribe and Ambience together rather than as substitutes. Content analysis identified documentation efficiency (21/34) and note detail capture (21/34) as the most emphasized strengths, with accuracy limitations (10/34) and workflow friction (6/34) as recurring concerns. A small subset (3/34) described the platform surfacing diagnoses or actions they might otherwise have missed. Findings are favorable but limited by small size, repeated responses, and positively framed items.

items.title: A Process-and-Rules-Based Software Development Lifecycle
items.abstract: A Process-and-Rules-Based Software Development Lifecycle Engineering Software for Correctness, Human Effectiveness and Continuous Improvement This paper sets out a process-and-rules-based approach to the software development lifecycle. It is a practitioner methodology drawn from professional experience in systems design and software engineering, and tested again through practical work with artificial intelligence. The premise is that business software should be designed around the processes it must perform, the rules governing them and the outcomes it must produce. Rules are held as governed data, owned by the organisation and applied by an engine, and are not scattered through code. The methodology separates specification, implementation and independent verification. Expected results are fixed and proven before construction, as an exact result or a stated tolerance: if you cannot know the results, you do not know the problem. Two testing regimes are used together: predetermined positive and negative testing through to user acceptance by the business and production support, and complete-population testing with every input accounted for. Efficiency is specified and tested as unit run time, system throughput, break load and scaling with hardware. The paper also covers a single definition separating defects from changes, eight quality measures assessed separately, human interface engineering, the distinction between education and training, and the role of AI as implementer, analyst and delegated process owner. It argues that the cost that matters is the cost per successful line of code, not the cost per line written. It is a methodology, not a rule book. It reports practice, one proposition and one case from current work, and does not claim that its effectiveness has been demonstrated by controlled comparison. AI tools were used in the development, criticism and drafting of the paper; responsibility for its propositions rests with the author.

items.title: A retrieval-augmented local large language model for ICD-10-CM terminology mapping of clinical signs and symptoms
items.abstract: Accurately mapping clinical signs and symptoms (S&S) from free text to ICD-10-CM codes is essential for early cancer detection, phenotyping, and risk-prediction modeling. However, manual coding is labor-intensive, and automated models often generate invalid or hallucinated codes. This study evaluates whether grounding a large language model (LLM) in the full ICD-10-CM catalog through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves accuracy and reliability compared with an LLM operating without retrieval. Using 200 clinical notes containing 545 human-labeled S&S, we compared an LLM-only baseline, a retrieval-only voting baseline, and a RAG-LLM model. Eight domain-specific and general embedding models produced dense vectors for all 98,186 ICD-10-CM codes. For each symptom, up to 40 candidate codes were retrieved by cosine similarity and incorporated into the model prompt for final selection. Performance was evaluated at the three-character ICD-10 block level against human annotations, with expert adjudication of non-matching cases. Code validity and raw description consistency were evaluated using the official ICD-10-CM reference. The RAG-LLM model achieved 85.87% three-character ICD-10-CM match accuracy, outperforming the LLM-only baseline (72.11%) and the retrieval-only voting baseline (55.60%). After exploratory adjudication, 98.90% of RAG-LLM outputs were considered clinically acceptable S&S mappings. Paired McNemar tests showed significant improvements over both baselines. The RAG-LLM model also reduced invalid ICD-10-CM code generation from 9.91% in the LLM-only baseline to 1.10%. This proof-of-concept study shows that retrieval-guided LLM candidate selection can improve symptom/sign-level ICD-10-CM terminology mapping on MTsamples. The RAG-LLM model improved both three-character and full-code matching while reducing invalid ICD-10-CM code generation. These findings support further evaluation of retrieval-guided LLM mapping as a preprocessing approach for symptom-based phenotyping research, but additional validation is needed before use in real-world EHR workflows, billing-grade coding, or downstream disease-prediction models.

items.title: A Review of Mechanistic and Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Models for Predicting Pesticide Fate and Transport in Soil and Water
items.abstract: Global pesticide use exceeded 3.7 million tonnes in 2023, and residues that persist beyond the treated field drive diffuse soil, surface water, and groundwater contamination linked to ecological harm and an estimated 150,000 pesticide poisoning deaths annually. Because field monitoring of pesticide fate across every soil, climate, and hydrological setting is logistically and financially infeasible at regulatory scale, predictive modelling has become the primary tool for estimating environmental concentrations and associated risk. This review traces the development of the field from traditional process-based mechanisms to hybrid AI frameworks by synthesizing 81 peer-reviewed and technical sources from an initial pool of 1,450 records screened across Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect (2005–2026). We look at the physicochemical and degradation principles that determine the fate of pesticides; the deterministic, mechanistic, process-based, empirical, and statistical models that support the current regulatory risk assessment; the hydrological and transport models that function at the soil profile to watershed scale; and the expanding array of machine learning, deep learning, fuzzy logic, GIS, remote sensing, and IoT-enabled techniques that are transforming precision agriculture and prediction. Case studies from India and other countries demonstrate real-world uses in addition to ongoing limitations in data accessibility and cross-context transferability. We point out important gaps, such as persistent data scarcity in low- and middle-income regions, limited coupling of fate models to downscaled climate projections, and inadequate integration of explainable AI to foster regulatory trust. We identify calibration and validation, particularly probabilistic uncertainty quantification, as essential to the responsible use of both conventional and data-driven models. We conclude that creating accurate, transferable pesticide prediction systems that support the Sustainable Development Goals and safeguard human and environmental health requires combining mechanistic understanding with hybrid, physics-informed AI and climate-resilient precision agriculture technologies.

items.title: A review of unmanned aerial vehicle design and artificial intelligence methods for autonomous flight
items.abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles have progressed from remotely controlled military targets to versatile platforms serving industrial, scientific and civil roles. This narrative review traces that progression from the unmanned balloons of 1849 to autonomous rotorcraft operating beyond Earth. The quadrotor architecture is examined in detail, covering frame configuration, propulsion, flight control and navigation, power systems, sensing payloads and telemetry, with attention to the trade-offs that couple these subsystems and constrain endurance, payload and controller complexity. This review analyses where structural and algorithmic concerns intersect. Integrating nonlinear deep learning estimators with deterministic flight controllers, as fault-tolerant designs require, raises problems of closed-loop stability, inference latency and actuator transients during fault handover. Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning, trained centrally but executed locally on each vehicle, allows drones to coordinate with far less communication than fixed waypoint schemes need. A comparative assessment of convolutional networks, vision transformers and reinforcement learning evaluates each against the accuracy, onboard inference cost and robustness that airborne deployment demands. Missions such as NASA’s Ingenuity Mars Helicopter and the planned Dragonfly rotorcraft demonstrate autonomous flight under constraints that preclude direct control. The review closes by examining the safety, energy, privacy and ethical limitations that condition responsible deployment.

items.title: A Systematic Review on Lung Cancer Detection Using Machine Learning Techniques
items.abstract: Lung cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, highlighting the urgent need for accurate and reliable diagnostic methods. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) have made it a valuable tool for lung cancer diagnosis by leveraging various imaging modalities, datasets, preprocessing techniques, feature extraction methods, classification algorithms, and segmentation strategies. This literature review systematically examines the application of ML techniques in lung cancer detection, emphasizing the progress achieved across these areas. It also identifies the strengths and limitations of existing ML approaches, underscoring the need for multi-modal learning, hybrid artificial intelligence models, and heterogeneous datasets to improve diagnostic performance. Despite notable progress, challenges in early detection remain, warranting further research on integrating deep learning with radiomics, multi-scale analysis, and enhanced feature representation to strengthen early diagnosis and support more effective clinical decision-making.

items.title: A Taxonomy of Confabulations and the Perception-Reality Gap in LLM-Assisted Immersive Scene Editing
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are being increasingly integrated into immersive environments and design workflows, providing application prospects in areas such as rapid scene prototyping for non-expert users and scene understanding capabilities for accessibility design. While many workflows that incorporate LLMs in immersive spaces are proposed, such systems can exhibit errors, potentially resulting in frustration, loss of user trust, and compromised user safety. This paper studies the underexplored area of LLM confabulations in immersive 3D scene editing contexts. Through an exploratory study with 24 non-expert users, we construct a taxonomy of the different types of confabulation observed in LLM-assisted immersive 3D scene editing. We report their prevalence and perceived disruptiveness, and define the construct perception-reality gap to help understand the gap between the actual and perceived occurrence of confabulations. We highlight the observed saturation of confabulation awareness under load and conclude by discussing design implications for confabulation mitigation in future LLM-assisted systems in immersive 3D scenes.

items.title: A Usage Snapshot: AI for Oral Communication Development in the Workplace
items.abstract: Oral communication skills remain critical for the workplace at a time of significant technological disruption. While anecdotal evidence suggests workers are using AI to develop these skills through methods such as role-play and feedback, there is a lack of empirical data on how widespread this usage is. This study surveyed working adults in Aotearoa New Zealand (N = 478) on their use of AI to build oral communication skills. Findings show 26.2% had used AI for this purpose in the past six months, just behind the two most common non-AI methods. Where respondents named an AI tool they had used, these were almost all general-purpose tools such as ChatGPT or Copilot, instead of specialised AI communication tools. Usage was predominantly text-based rather than voice-based and centred more on preparation than on practice or reflection. This suggests a potential gap between assistance and skill development, with AI used more to prepare what to say than to practise how to say it or strengthen the underlying skills.

items.title: AdapTest: Supporting Designers in Authoring and Evaluating Environmentally Responsive User Interfaces for Extended Reality
items.abstract: Extended Reality (XR) headsets increasingly host familiar 2D user interfaces as windows floating in physical environments. However, their usability depends on environmental conditions that designers cannot fully control. Current design workflows often separate how a variant is designed from how it actually looks in the target environment. We present AdapTest , an in-situ authoring and testing tool that lets designers select interface elements, define when and how they change, compare the resulting variations, and test their activation without coding. Based on prior research and a formative study with 12 interface designers, the system targets three key environmental variables: distance, lighting, and occlusion. We evaluated AdapTest against a desktop design and in-headset preview workflow in a within-subjects study with 12 designers. Compared with the baseline, designers accounted for a wider range of environmental factors, addressed more overlapping conditions, and repeatedly tested and revised their designs in place; there were no significant differences in workload or usability despite longer sessions. Our work contributes an integrated, designer-centered approach to adapting, comparing, and validating environmentally responsive XR user interfaces.

items.title: Adaptive and Explainable Decision Support for Resilient Industrial Rail Operations: A Human-Centric DMAIC–Machine Learning Framework
items.abstract: Industry 5.0 calls for decision-support systems that are human-centric, resilient, and transparent. However, in bulk-material logistics, predictive models are often developed as static tools, with limited attention to process structure, interpretability, and changing operating conditions. This study proposes a decision-support framework that combines the DMAIC cycle, machine learning (ML), explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), and human-in-the-loop model management, and applies it to rail unloading at a phosphate-handling facility. DMAIC was first used to structure process knowledge and identify the main drivers of daily throughput, including train frequency, wagon filling conditions, unloading duration, and operational losses. ML models were then evaluated for early prediction of final daily throughput, using only information available after the first train, with and without recent historical context. Adding historical features reduced validation MAE across all four tabular algorithms, with V2-XGBoost reaching a validation MAE of 2043 T/J and an RMSE of 2368 T/J. On the final chronological test period, however, all fixed ML models returned negative R2 values. Between the training and test periods, mean throughput increased from 19,070 to 22,233 T/J, and the proportion of seven-train days rose from 16.5% to 68.1%, indicating a marked regime shift. SHAP analysis was used to explain model behavior at the global and local levels, including regime-dependent predictive relationships. Based on these findings, we outline a human-supervised architecture linking early prediction, explanation, performance monitoring, and model review, in which operators and managers retain final decision authority. The study highlights the importance of evaluating predictive reliability under changing operating conditions in industrial logistics.

items.title: Advancing Interdisciplinary Approaches to Inclusive Online Safety Research
items.abstract: Online safety is a pressing concern, yet its harms fall unevenly, particularly on communities whose needs mainstream safety tools were not designed to meet, such as women and gender-diverse people, LGBTQ+ communities, culturally and linguistically diverse communities, and people with disability. At the same time, artificial intelligence is reshaping this landscape as both a source of new harms and a proposed remedy. These challenges are hard to address because online safety research remains fragmented across HCI sub-fields and adjacent disciplines, with limited communication between them. This workshop brings together researchers, designers, policymakers, industry practitioners, and community advocates, from within and beyond HCI, to examine two questions: which groups are most vulnerable to online harms and need greater attention, and in what ways does AI enhance online safety or create and intensify online risks? Through structured discussion and collaborative activities organised around case studies and scenarios of exclusion, participants will identify communities that need greater attention, interrogate the dual role of AI, and build interdisciplinary networks and a shared research agenda, advancing collaborative research directions within Australia and beyond toward more inclusive and effective responses to online safety.

items.title: Adversarial Malware Detection Using Feature Contribution Difference Analysis with Kernel SHAP
items.abstract: Adversarial malware evades machine-learning-based detection by modifying its feature vector while preserving its malicious functionality. As attack methods continue to diversify, learning all possible adversarial patterns using conventional adversarial training has become impractical. However, because adversarial malware must retain its malicious functionality, certain intrinsic characteristics are common across diverse attacks. Based on this observation, we propose a two-stage adversarial malware detection method that leverages explainable artificial intelligence to analyze feature contributions in the prediction process. In the first stage, a neural network classifier performs the initial detection. In the second stage, Kernel SHAP is used to quantify each feature’s contribution to the model’s prediction, and the average contribution difference between benign software and malware is computed. The proposed method assigns higher weights to features with small contribution differences, which tend to exhibit high contributions when malware is present, and computes a maliciousness score to redetect adversarial samples that are misclassified as benign. Experimental results on Android application datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing approaches across four representative adversarial attacks (fast gradient sign method, JSMA, Mimicry, and Pointwise) without explicitly learning attack-specific characteristics.

items.title: Adversarial prompt detection via contrastive dual-encoder transformer for zero-day jailbreak defense based on AdverSentinel-LLM model
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have become core elements of current artificial intelligence applications yet are highly susceptible to adversarial prompt attacks such as jailbreaks that compromise safety alignment. Current defense mechanisms rely predominantly on fixed rule-based filters or single-encoder classifiers with limited generalizability to new, zero-day jailbreak signatures. This paper presents AdverSentinel-LLM, a novel adversarial prompt detector based on a Contrastive Dual-Encoder Transformer (CDET) architecture trained to identify malicious prompts in real time, including zero-day jailbreak attacks. The CDET architecture maintains two independent representation spaces—one encoding prompt semantics and one encoding structured threat patterns—trained jointly under a supervised contrastive objective that explicitly pushes adversarial embeddings away from benign clusters, enabling zero-day generalization to unseen attack vectors via contrastive disentanglement. The framework comprises two parallel transformer encoders: a Prompt Semantic Encoder (PSE) that learns deep contextual representations of input prompts and a Threat Pattern Encoder (TPE) that learns discriminative representations of known adversarial attack patterns. A supervised contrastive learning objective encourages separation between adversarial and benign embeddings, enabling zero-day generalization to unseen attack vectors. We additionally incorporate a Dynamic Threat Memory Bank (DTMB) with prototype pruning and rejuvenation to prevent stagnation, and an Anomaly-Aware Gating Mechanism (AAGM) for context-sensitive detection threshold modulation. Extensive experiments on AdvBench, JailbreakBench, ToxicChat, and PromptSafety-Bench demonstrate state-of-the-art performance with an F1-score of 0.967, detection accuracy of 97.3%, and a zero-day detection rate of 94.8%, with the contribution of every architectural element verified by ablation studies and preliminary evidence of cross-model transferability demonstrated across adversarial prompt distributions independently curated against GPT-4, LLaMA-3, Claude-3, and Gemini-Pro backends; a controlled matched-prompt evaluation is deferred to future work.

items.title: Agentic AI for knowledge-driven hull-form design in high-speed autonomous surface vessels
items.abstract: High-speed autonomous surface vessels require hull forms that balance resistance, running attitude, hydrodynamic stability, and mission-related constraints. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) supports detailed assessment of planing-hull performance, but knowledge generated by individual parametric studies is rarely reused in subsequent design projects. This paper proposes a knowledge-driven agentic AI framework that transforms CFD-derived evidence into reusable design support for early-stage hull-form development. Unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes simulations are conducted for straked-hull configurations, building a database of deadrise angle effects on resistance, trim, sinkage, pressure distribution, and wave characteristics. An LLM-based design manager retrieves relevant historical cases, interprets hydrodynamic trends, weighs recommendations from multiple advisory tools, and selects candidate deadrise angles through an auditable reasoning trace. The framework integrates case retrieval, Savitsky-based physics priors, Bayesian optimisation, a CFD-derived oracle, and episodic reflection, with a human designer retained in the loop. The agent identifies the resistance-optimal deadrise angle subject to running trim and sinkage constraints, using 60% fewer oracle evaluations than an exhaustive parametric sweep at 30 kn. Out-of-library validation at 45 kn confirms the efficiency advantage under genuine extrapolation, locating the optimum after four evaluations versus nine for the exhaustive sweep. The study demonstrates how CFD campaigns can be converted into reusable engineering memory, providing a basis for future agentic hull-form design systems.

items.title: AGENTIC ST-T1024: A17 Detecting Emergent Collective Behaviour in Multi- Agent Systems. From Individual Agent Control to Collective Agency Detection. An Open Research and Architectural Proposal
items.abstract: The rapid development of agentic artificial intelligence introduces a challenge that extends beyond the control of individual AI agents.Multiple agents, each operating within an individually defined operational perimeter, mayinteract in ways that produce collective behaviour. Such behaviour may include recurringinteraction patterns, the propagation of objectives, shared strategies and coordinatedoperations. In some circumstances, collective coordination may emerge without an explicit instruction to coordinate. This raises an important architectural question:Can a collection of individually controlled agents develop collective behaviour thatexceeds the operational perimeter defined by humans? The ST-T1024 A17 proposal addresses this question as a complementary researchextension to the existing A1–A16 architecture. Its initial design proposes a Spiking Neural Network (SNN) for temporal pattern learning and detection, a Learning Set (LS) containing previously identified swarm sequences, and acontinuously updated memory mechanism (MEMO) for observing current and past agentactivity. The central research hypothesis is that coordination may produce what this paper calls Enhanced Repetitions: recurring patterns that are reinforced, extended and propagatedthrough interactions among agents. A17 proposes a Boolean detection output:● SWARM = 1: identify the participating agents as a detected collective operation andprevent them from continuing that coordinated operation.● SWARM = 0: continue observing and memorizing the sequences. The proposal does not assume that coordination is necessarily malicious. Detecting collective behaviour, determining whether it exceeds human authorization, and determining whether it is harmful are separate questions. A17 is presented as an open research and architectural proposal. Its algorithms, learningmethodology, memory parameters, detection performance and implementation remainsubjects for independent investigation and experimental validation. The governing principle is simple: humans define the operational perimeter; agentsoperate within it; collective agency must not redefine it.

items.abstract: This seminar report explores the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and deep learning techniques for preliminary skin disease screening using smartphone images. The report covers image acquisition, preprocessing, AI model inference, and the importance of communicating predictions responsibly. It also highlights key challenges, including image quality, skin-tone representation, data privacy, class imbalance, and the risk of incorrect predictions. items.title: AI Chatbot UI/UX Design for Sam Ratulangi University KIP-Kuliah Re-Registration
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has fundamentally reshaped our reality, influencing the way we work, learn, and communicate. This technology enables informed decision-making by analyzing data through learning, reasoning, and self-correction. In Android application development, implementing AI requires an optimal User Interface (UI) and User Experience (UX) to bridge the complexity of the system with user needs. This research addresses the challenges in the KIP-Kuliah scholarship re-registration process at Sam Ratulangi University, where students frequently encounter difficulties in accessing centralized information, leading to inadequate document preparation and other administrative issues. Using the Multimedia Development Life Cycle (MDLC) method, this study develops an Android-based virtual assistant application ("Tian") integrated with a Laravel back-end and the Google Gemini API. Initial prototype evaluation was conducted through functional testing on three Android devices and a 5-point Likert questionnaire distributed to 10 KIP-Kuliah recipient students from the 2025 cohort. Teknologi ini mampu mendukung pengambilan keputusan dengan menganalisis data melalui kemampuan learning, reasoning, dan self-correction. items.title: AI for Spiritual Growth: A Collaborative Ethnography with Professing Christians
items.abstract: Spiritual AI is a nascent area of HCI research exploring how generative AI can augment spiritual experiences. Research to date has focused on speculative design, but actual AI use for spiritual purposes remains unexplored. To address this gap, this research explored how AI is used in daily life, specifically for spiritual growth in a Christian tradition. This research was inspired by and based on the first author’s experience, as well as collaborative ethnographic research with 20 participants who publicly identify as Christians. Our findings show how AI was used for spiritual practices across three areas – growth in knowledge, faith, and godliness – and how AI both supported and conflicted with practices such as Bible study and prayer. Based on these findings, we propose a revised notion of spiritual AI that is grounded in lived spiritual practice, rather than augmented experience, and present an agenda for future HCI research.

items.title: AI in the Room: Lessons from Generative AI-Driven Co-Design in Health and Care
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in health and care for clinical support and to mediate collaboration within design processes. While co-design is well established in health and care, how generative AI-driven tools influence inclusivity, participation, sense-making and power dynamics remains underexplored. Our research explored the role of generative AI in co-design activities in high-stakes health and care settings. We report findings from an HCI conference workshop involving ten researchers and practitioners engaged in health and care intervention design. Activities were structured using the Double Diamond Framework supported by four generative AI tools. Our findings showed key roles specific generative AI tools can play across the different stages of the design process. However, participants identified challenges that may introduce bias and constrain co-design practice. The findings highlighted that strong human mediation is essential for effective AI-assisted co-design enabling reflective, inclusive and responsible design practice in health and care.
